summary: The core is one flat board-level netlist in williams2.vhd. It has a shared CPU/blitter/video bus, VRAM split into six nibble-wide RAM chips addressed through the IC60 7649 decoder PROM, a cycle-stepped blitter that takes the bus through 6809 HALT/BA/BS, and per-pixel shift registers fed by raster counters. MAME does the blit in one instant C loop, treats video RAM as a flat 48K array, leaves the IC60 PROM unconnected, and draws the background with a tilemap; the core follows none of these. Only the register addresses and bit semantics are shared, and a correct core has to share those anyway.

findings.signal: IC60 decoder PROM drives VRAM addressing and chip select
findings.mame_ref: williams/williams.cpp:ROM_START(tshoot) marks 7649.ic60 'not hooked up'; common_map maps 0x0000-0xbfff as linear RAM
findings.note: Bus address bits 15-8 go into the 7649 PROM. Its bits 5-0 form the VRAM column address and bits 7-6 pick which of three RAM banks gets the write. MAME skips this PROM entirely.

findings.signal: VRAM as six 4-bit RAM chips read in parallel
findings.note: Video RAM is six separate 16Kx4 instances (three banks, high and low nibble). One video access reads all six at once, giving 6 pixels per CPU microsecond. MAME instead reads a flat byte array at source[(x/2)*256].

findings.signal: Blitter as bus master via 6809 HALT/BA/BS, one read/write per bus slot
findings.note: The blitter raises HALT, waits for BA and BS, and then does one source read in the graph_access slot and one destination write in the CPU slot. Slow mode toggles blit_go. MAME runs nested for-y/for-x loops instantly and charges an estimated icount penalty.

findings.signal: Blit transparency and nibble masking as RAM write inhibits
findings.note: Even/odd pixel suppression and the transparency flag drive blit_wr_inh_h and blit_wr_inh_l, which gate the write enables of the high and low nibble RAMs. MAME does a read-modify-write with a keepmask. The core's approach is how separate nibble chips would behave on the board.

findings.signal: Raster counters and fixed bus time slots
findings.note: A 6-pixel phase counter splits each microsecond into CPU, ROM, video and graphics-ROM slots. An hcnt (0-63) / vcnt (252-511) chain then drives every address mux, and the video counter readback at CBE0 returns vcnt directly.

findings.signal: Background scroll as tile-map counter plus fine-scroll pixel delay line
findings.note: Coarse scroll is added into the map RAM column counter. Fine scroll picks a tap on an 11-stage bg pixel delay line, and tile flip reverses the shift direction. MAME computes a single scrollx=(x&7)+(x>>3)*6 and hands it to a TILEMAP_SCAN_COLS tilemap with TILE_FLIPX.

findings.signal: Per-pixel FG/BG priority at the palette RAM address mux
findings.note: The palette RAM address is muxed per pixel: a nonzero FG nibble wins, otherwise the BG pixel with bank and vcnt(7:5) bits. The palette RAMs' bytes go straight out as RGBI. MAME draws the whole tilemap first and then overdraws FG pens per frame, converting colors through calc_col.

The PIA CA1 input is tied to the vcnt=240 decode and CB1 to vcnt bit 5 (the 4ms tick). The two PIAs are wired pin to pin to the sound board's PIA (CB2 trigger, CB1 ack), not built around MAME-style callbacks.

findings.signal: Gun Gray encoding as a lookup ROM
findings.note: A 64-entry table gives the same result as MAME's (d ^ (d>>1)). It looks like a PROM rather than C, but the function is fixed either way.

findings.signal: Memory map, bank select and blitter register layout
findings.note: Address decodes and register offsets match MAME, as any correct core must. The bank decode is written as explicit page-value cases, not MAME's (data&6)>>1 view/bank scheme.

findings.signal: Sound board as a 6800 + PIA + RAM/ROM netlist
findings.note: A small chip-level board with its own clock divider and address decode. Little board-specific logic to judge, and nothing in it mirrors williamssound.cpp classes.
